neighbours.label: Verbs of handing something over to an audience or recipient: ' give', ' presented'/' presents', ' grant' in active or reduced-relative use (give a talk, the facts presented, grant access); quiet for receiving or attending verbs in the same frame
fire: Next month the author will give a reading at the town library.
The figures presented in the appendix cover only the last quarter.
The ministry can grant an exemption to small farms.
Our guides are happy to give suggestions about local restaurants.
The evidence presented at the hearing surprised the judge.
The trust reserves the right to grant entry to members only.
Every spring the choir presents a concert of new works to the town.
A nurse will give instructions to the family before discharge.
quiet: Next month the author will attend a reading at the town library.
The figures gathered in the appendix cover only the last quarter.
The ministry can refuse an exemption to small farms.
Our guides are happy to hear suggestions about local restaurants.
The evidence examined at the hearing surprised the judge.
The trust reserves the right to deny entry to non-members.
Every spring the choir rehearses a concert of new works in the hall.
A nurse will take instructions from the doctor before discharge.

notes: Card: ' give' x9, ' presented' x4, ' given' x4, ' grant' x2, ' presents' x2, ' show' x2. Probes: 'will give a lecture' 0.52, 'data presented in' 0.50, 'may grant a permit' 0.66; 'will attend a lecture' 0.02, 'data collected in' 0.04, 'was given a medal' 0.17.
